newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at record high after merger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at record high after merger.

text.p: Swedish share prices ended at record high levels on Wednesday, supported by positive sentiment after Tuesday's news about a merger of banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken.
But prices came off day highs late in the session on a sluggish New York market.
Stockholm general index rises 0.50 percent to a record of 2,662.47 in heavy turnover of 7.56 billion cronws.
Drugs company Astra fell 1.5 crowns to 358.5 crowns after coming off day highs late in the session. Astra presented a 10 percent rise in 1996 profits in line with market expectations.
Automotive group Volvo slipped one to 179 after releasing 1996 earnings, saying pre-tax profit rose nine percent to 14.2 billion crowns.
The forestry sector fell 0.16 percent. MoDo showed a 44 percent slump in 1996 earnings and ended flat at 228.
The bank sector continued to post gains amid speculation of further restructuring. Swedbank leaped 14.5 to 154, while S-E-Banken gained 4.5 crowns to end at 80.
Building company NCC rose eight to 97.5 and Siab 3.5 crowns to 54.5 after announcing a merger.
